tagline: SEO, PPC, and competitive research toolkit built on large web datasets.
verdictSummary: A small rank tracker and technical site auditor for a domain you own is a real build. What can't be reproduced is Semrush's actual product: keyword, backlink, competitor, and SERP data collected from crawling the web at scale over years — no personal script recreates a dataset like that.
coreLoopDIY: A scheduled tracker for your own keywords via a SERP API, a technical crawl of your own site, and your own Search Console data pulled in alongside it.
whatYouLose: competitor intelligence on domains you don't own
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for market and competitive data that a solo builder cannot cheaply or legally recreate — the dashboards are the easy part, the dataset behind them is not.
notes: An important 'no': naming the data moat plainly here keeps the rest of the catalogue honest about what a personal build can and can't reproduce.
prompt:
Build a rank and site-health tracker limited to domains you actually own — not a general SEO platform. A scheduled job that checks a chosen list of keywords against a real SERP API (there are several with an affordable tier; do not scrape Google's results pages directly) and stores position and ranking URL per day, with a simple report showing movement over time. Pull your own click and impression data for free from the Google Search Console API for properties you control. Run a technical crawl limited to your own domain flagging broken links, missing or duplicate titles and descriptions, redirect chains, and slow pages. Send a summary report only when something actually moved — a meaningful position swing, new broken links — rather than a constant stream of noise.

Do not attempt competitor keyword gaps, a backlink database, or traffic estimates for sites you don't own — none of that data can be self-collected without crawling the entire web continuously, which is exactly the infrastructure the subscription pays for.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Semrush data — tracked keywords, competitor research?
faq.a: Your tracked keyword list, yes, that's just a text file you maintain yourself. Historical keyword and backlink data cannot be exported or rebuilt; it only exists inside Semrush's own crawl and licensed datasets.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The report is a simple web page, so checking it on a phone works, but there's no app and no alerting beyond the scheduled email summary.

faq.q: What does it actually cost to run?
faq.a: A SERP API's affordable tier plus hosting, typically a small monthly cost well under Semrush's own pricing — Search Console access itself is free.

faq.q: What's the one thing that genuinely doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Anyone else's site. You can track and audit your own domain thoroughly; you cannot see a competitor's keyword gaps or backlink profile — that visibility only exists because Semrush already crawled it, continuously, for years.

faq.q: What's the best free Semrush alternative?
faq.a: OpenSEO is the best free Semrush alternative. It covers keyword research, rank tracking, competitor insights and backlinks through DataForSEO's paid API, at a cost per request. Pair it with SerpBear and Seonaut, and keep Semrush for the depth of its database, PPC and SERP history and traffic estimates.

faq.q: Can I replace Semrush's site audit and rank tracking for free?
faq.a: Yes, for a site you own. Seonaut crawls your site and lists issues, and SerpBear tracks your keyword rankings daily. Neither gives keyword volumes, backlinks or competitor data.

alternativesIntro: The best free Semrush alternative is OpenSEO: it covers keyword research, rank tracking, competitor insights and backlinks. It buys all its data from a paid API (DataForSEO), per request, so it costs money at volume and has no index of its own. Add SerpBear for daily rank tracking and Seonaut for site audits. For a few sites you own, that covers a lot of the $139.95 SEO Pro plan. Keep Semrush if you need the depth of its database, its PPC and SERP history or its traffic estimates.

alternativeNotes.open-seo: Covers keyword research, rank tracking, competitor insights and backlinks, driven by DataForSEO's paid API. It has no index of its own, so coverage and freshness are DataForSEO's.
alternativeNotes.serpbear: Tracks keyword rankings daily for your own domain. It has no crawl, no backlink data and no competitor database.
alternativeNotes.seonaut: Crawls a site and lists issues with page reports. It has no rank tracking and no backlink data.
alternativeNotes.seomacroscope: Runs a technical crawl of a site you control. It has no rank tracking and no backlink or keyword database.
